request.prompt:
You are the Stage 4 Synthesist. Turn one promoted failure-mode cluster into an honest, human-gated remedy proposal.

Most frustrations do not deserve a skill. Route in this strict preference order: (1) `claude-md`, a one/two-line standing rule; (2) `hook`, or an equivalent mechanical setting, when enforcement is possible; (3) `skill`, only for a genuinely procedural or multi-step remedy; (4) `benchmark-only` when the failure is model-level and no instruction can fix it. Choose the cheapest remedy that fixes the failure mode: every skill consumes the user's context budget. `benchmark-only` is an honorable outcome, never manufacture a remedy merely to feel useful.

If the only sensible remedy target is Codex-side (`AGENTS.md` or `~/.codex/skills`), use `benchmark-only` and state that Codex installation is out of v1 in `note`.

You must check every existing-remedy digest below. State a `dedup` item for each one with `clear` or `overlap`. Merge bias is law: if any verdict is `overlap`, this is a revision of that existing remedy, never a sibling. Set `overlap_action.revises` to the exact existing reference.

For a `skill`, write a kebab-case name and a concrete auto-invocation description beginning `Use when ...`; this description is the trigger. The body must be substantive Markdown. For `claude-md`, select `global` or `project`; project target requires its project name. For `hook`, give a Claude Code event and a command sketch. For `benchmark-only`, explain the measurement-only outcome in `note`.

The upstream classifier deliberately over-merges. You may split ONLY in this stage, and only when the evidence is genuinely heterogeneous. A split must provide proposals of the same shape, partition every promoted incident exactly once, and leave none orphaned. Otherwise return one proposal covering the group.

TAXONOMY GIST:
destructive-action: deleted/overwrote/reset without care

PROMOTED EVIDENCE:
BEGIN PROMOTED EVIDENCE incident_id=2 project=aurora
One-liner: Deleted content without obtaining user consent first
Preceding request:
The constraint from the opening note was discarded again.

Agent activity digest:
Assistant: Synthetic acknowledgement.

Frustrated message:
What are you doing? You deleted the fake migration without asking.

Following exchange:

END PROMOTED EVIDENCE

EXISTING SKILLS (name and description only):
- skill:$HOME/.claude/skills/fake-verify-before-claim/SKILL.md | name=fake-verify-before-claim | description=Use when a completion claim requires verification.

S2S-MANAGED CLAUDE.MD BLOCKS:
- claude-md:$HOME/.claude/CLAUDE.md#1 | # Fake Release Discipline

Before reporting a fake release as complete, run its declared verification
command and report the result plainly.

PENDING OR INSTALLED S2S PROPOSALS:
- (none)

structured_output.failure_statement: The agent deletes content (e.g., a migration, file, or data) without asking for user confirmation first, even when a prior instruction in the session already told it not to.

remedy_content.command_sketch: A PreToolUse hook script that inspects the pending Bash command against a destructive-pattern regex list (e.g. `rm -rf?`, `DROP TABLE`, `TRUNCATE`, `DELETE FROM`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f`, `git push --force`, redirect-overwrites onto existing files). If a match is found and the transcript shows no explicit prior user confirmation for that exact action, the hook exits with a blocking decision (exit code 2 with a reason string) so Claude Code surfaces a permission prompt asking the user to confirm before the deletion runs, instead of silently executing it.
remedy_content.note: Scope the hook to Bash tool calls; do not attempt to intercept every Edit/Write since most content overwrites there are benign — the destructive cases (rm, DROP, TRUNCATE, force-reset) are the ones with real irrecoverable blast radius.

structured_output.routing_rationale: The incident describes an unambiguous destructive action (deleting a migration) taken without user consent, and the preceding-request note ("the constraint from the opening note was discarded again") indicates a plain-language instruction not to do this was already in play and was ignored. That rules out claude-md as sufficient on its own — a standing instruction already existed and failed. Destructive filesystem/DB actions triggered via Bash (rm, DROP, TRUNCATE, DELETE FROM, git reset --hard/clean) are mechanically detectable via pattern match before execution, so a PreToolUse hook that gates on those patterns and forces explicit confirmation is the cheapest remedy that actually enforces the missing behavior, ranking above skill (this isn't a multi-step procedure) and above claude-md alone (already tried and failed per the incident).
